pages.name: Quick Start
pages.content:
Close Combat

  1. When positional enforcement is enabled, place the attacker and defender in the same grid space.
  2. Target exactly one defender.
  3. Click an equipped melee weapon, choose an action from a Close Combat Skill roll, or use Take Action on the Character sheet.
  4. If the action can be Blocked, resolve the declaration card before rolling the attack.
  5. Choose an aimed hit location only when deliberately accepting its modifier.
  6. Push or accept the final roll, then use the available chat-card button to apply damage or the action outcome.

The system derives stance, defenseless-target, and hit-location rules from the selected tokens. Keep token positions and Actor statuses current before rolling. Worlds using abstract maps can disable the same-space requirement in World Rules and Display → Rules Automation.

pages.name: Position, Stance, and Targets
pages.content:
Position and Stance

By default, close-combat attacks require the attacker and defender to occupy the same grid space. The system stops the attack if both tokens can be measured and are in different spaces. Cover does not protect a target in close combat.

Optional Positioning

A GM can open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings → World Rules and Display and disable Require Same Grid Space for Close Combat. Close-combat attacks and maneuvers can then proceed between targeted Actors in different hexes or squares. This is intended for abstract maps and theatre-of-the-mind positioning. It does not make distant combatants count as sharing a space for ranged same-space modifiers.

Prone Combatants

  • A prone attacker receives an automatic −2.
  • Attacking a prone target receives +2.
  • If a prone attacker attacks a standing target, the hit location is automatically the legs.

Defenseless Targets

A defenseless or unaware target gives +3. This replaces, rather than stacks with, the +2 for a prone target. The roll dialog lists every automatic rules modifier so players can verify what was applied.

pages.name: Aimed Blows
pages.content:
Aimed Blows

For an attack that rolls hit location, use the Aimed or Called Hit Location menu in the roll dialog. Choosing a location applies −2 and stores that location on the attack. The damage workflow then uses the chosen location instead of rolling one randomly.

Leave the menu at Random location for an ordinary attack. A forced rules result, such as a prone attacker striking a standing target, takes precedence and is shown on the roll card.

pages.name: Blocking
pages.content:
Blocking an Attack

Unarmed attacks, melee-weapon attacks, shoves, disarms, grapples, and diving blows can be Blocked.

  1. The attacker declares the action and target.
  2. The defender chooses whether to Block on the declaration card.
  3. A Block spends a Fast Action. If no Fast Action remains, an available Slow Action may be used.
  4. The defender makes and finishes the Block roll.
  5. The attacker makes and finishes the attack roll.
  6. Apply the Block from its chat card. Each Block success cancels one attack success.

Only attack successes left after the Block can inflict damage or apply an action outcome. A defender who cannot act cannot Block. A successful ambush opening can also prevent the target from Blocking that opening attack.

pages.name: Diving Blows
pages.content:
Diving Blow

A diving blow combines a Run and an unarmed attack in the same round.

  1. Use Run earlier in the current combat round.
  2. Move into the target's grid space and target that Actor. On an abstract map where the GM disabled positional enforcement, narratively establish that the attacker reached the target instead.
  3. Choose Diving Blow from Take Action or a Close Combat roll.
  4. Resolve any Block, then roll the attack with its automatic +2.

The attacker becomes prone as soon as the attack is rolled, whether it succeeds or fails. On a successful result, Apply Outcome also makes the target prone. The unarmed damage result remains available separately on the attack card.

pages.name: Shove and Disarm
pages.content:
Shove

Shove is a Fast Action and can be Blocked. It normally needs one remaining success. If the target's Strength is higher than the attacker's, it needs two. Apply Outcome makes the target prone and ends its close engagement.

Disarm

Disarm is a Fast Action and can be Blocked. After a successful roll, Apply Outcome asks which equipped item is being disarmed. A one-handed item requires one remaining success; a two-handed item requires two. The selected item is unequipped when the requirement is met.

pages.name: Grapple and Break Free
pages.content:
Grappling

Grapple is a Slow unarmed action and can be Blocked. On a successful result, Apply Outcome makes both combatants prone, marks the target as restrained, and links the two Actors. The grappled Actor must attempt Break Free; the grappler is limited to Grapple Attack until the grapple ends.

Breaking Free

Break Free is a Slow opposed Close Combat test. The system rolls the grappler's passive resistance without pushing and records its successes on the active Actor's roll card. Only the Actor attempting to break free may push. They must finish with more successes than the grappler; a tie fails. Apply Outcome appears only after a winning final result and clears both sides of the grapple.

A Grapple Attack is a Fast Action against the linked target. Water and drowning states can add further automated consequences. Keep both Actors accessible to the user resolving the outcome; if permissions prevent the counterpart from being updated, ask the GM to apply it.

pages.name: Retreating and Troubleshooting
pages.content:
Retreating

Use Retreat before leaving an engagement. On success, Apply Outcome ends the engagement. On failure, the roll card gives the opponent a Roll Free Attack button. The opponent chooses an equipped melee weapon or an unarmed attack. This immediate attack spends no action, cannot be Blocked, and then ends the retreating Actor's engagement.

Situational Help

Modifiers that cannot be determined from the canvas—such as allies helping, unusual terrain, or a ruling specific to the scene—remain available in the roll dialog or its general modifier field. Do not select prone or defenseless modifiers manually when they already appear under Automatic Rules Modifiers.

Troubleshooting

  • Same-space warning: move both tokens into the same grid space, or ask the GM whether positional enforcement should be disabled for this world.
  • No Block card: check that exactly one valid target is selected and that the opening attack does not prevent a Block.
  • Diving blow unavailable: use Run first in the same active combat round.
  • No outcome button: finish pushing and resolve the Block; unsuccessful actions intentionally show a failure message instead.
